findings.status: Blocking overall output/source-boundary and clean-sdist acceptance
findings.title: The rejected-output failure handler writes into the source checkout, and a later build accepts the leaked untracked receipt.
findings.observation: validate_package rejects in-checkout output outside ci-artifacts before creating its output directory. main nevertheless writes acceptance.json whenever that rejected output already exists and lacks a receipt. A subsequent actual default checker packages that generated file and exits 0. The manifest gate only checks forbidden path names and required Plato source presence; it does not bind other sdist payloads to the frozen Git tree. Empty source_status uses --untracked-files=no and therefore cannot prove the packaged inputs came only from the recorded source commit.

reproduction.guard_error: Output within the checkout must be under the excluded ci-artifacts path.

generated_receipt.error: Output within the checkout must be under the excluded ci-artifacts path.

findings.impact: A failed attempt to use an existing unsupported in-checkout output directory creates generated data outside the declared excluded output boundary. Normal default validation can then accept an archive with untracked generated payload while recording the same source commit and empty tracked-only status. The wheel remains identical, so rebuild/install checks cannot detect this sdist-only contamination.
required_changes: Reject invalid or pre-existing output directories without writing, creating or modifying any content in those directories. Write failure receipts only into a validated output directory successfully created and owned by the current invocation; checking output.is_dir() alone is insufficient.

Make clean-sdist acceptance bind every source member to the frozen Git tree and its bytes, with a narrow explicit allowance for backend-generated metadata. This source produces exactly 1,210 matching Git-tree members plus generated PKG-INFO, so that gate accepts both proven clean paths and rejects the observed untracked leak. Keep the actual manifest/hash receipts and treat tracked-only Git status as tracked status, not complete source cleanliness.

Add regressions for an existing unsupported in-checkout output directory, an existing output not owned by the invocation, and the checkout root: each must fail without changing any content. A subsequent default build must retain the proven clean manifest. Also inject an unrelated untracked sdist member and alter a tracked source payload to prove the source-binding gate fails while allowing verified generated metadata.

Preserve the generated docs/CI exclusions, existing forbidden-payload/metadata/source-coverage gates, locked build/runtime constraints, clean from-sdist rebuild, outside-checkout installed-wheel proof and publication boundary. Bind replacement receipts to the corrected source and send them to another fresh reviewer.
